title: What is a "circuit" in a DL model?

cues.en: Welcome to this section of the course.
cues.zh: 歡迎來到本章。

cues.en: Here I will teach you some methods for identifying organizing principles in a complex system that are
cues.zh: 這裡會介紹一些方法，根據少量維度、神經元的集合，

cues.en: based on small collections of dimensions, or neurons.
cues.zh: 辨識複雜系統中的組織原則。

cues.en: This is one level higher than looking at individual neurons or output dimensions, but it's also a bit
cues.zh: 這比觀察個別神經元或輸出維度，高一個層級，但也稍微

cues.en: more targeted and focused compared to looking at an entire layer or an entire embeddings.
cues.zh: 更有目標、更聚焦，相較於觀察整個層或整個嵌入

cues.en: Vector.
cues.zh: 向量而言。

cues.en: Circuit based analyses are really interesting and insightful, but they're also very tricky, both conceptually and methodologically.
cues.zh: 以迴路為基礎的分析，非常有意思、能帶來見解，但概念與方法上都很棘手。

cues.en: Conceptually, it's not even really clear what exactly a circuit is or should look like.
cues.zh: 概念上，甚至不太清楚迴路究竟是什麼，或應該長什麼樣子。

cues.en: It's also possible that circuits in complex systems, like language models, are so complex and dynamic
cues.zh: 也有可能，在語言模型這種複雜系統中，迴路非常複雜、動態，

cues.en: that the circuit architecture itself changes in different contexts and also methodologically.
cues.zh: 以至於迴路架構本身，會隨不同上下文改變。方法上也是如此，

cues.en: Statistically, it's quite difficult to identify circuits because, again, the activations are so dynamic and context dependent.
cues.zh: 從統計上辨識迴路很困難，因為活化高度動態，而且取決於上下文。

cues.en: Later in this section, I will also introduce you to the idea of latent constructs or components, which is both conceptually and methodologically also pretty tricky.
cues.zh: 本章後面，也會介紹潛在構念或成分的概念，同樣在概念與方法上，都相當棘手。

cues.en: So basically this section is state of the art.
cues.zh: 所以基本上，本章是最先進的研究內容，

cues.en: It's one of the more difficult areas of mechanistic interpretability, but I'm still going to try to
cues.zh: 是機制可解釋性比較困難的領域之一，但我仍會盡量

cues.en: make it an enjoyable and insightful learning experience, and I think you're going to enjoy it.
cues.zh: 讓它成為愉快、有啟發性的學習體驗，相信你會喜歡。

cues.en: I will start here by introducing some of the conceptual difficulties of circuit analyses.
cues.zh: 先介紹迴路分析的一些概念困難。

cues.en: Basically, the problem is that we don't really have a set definition of what a circuit means in systems
cues.zh: 基本問題是，對於那些迴路自行浮現的系統，

cues.en: where the circuits emerge on their own, either through biological or through statistical means.
cues.zh: 不論透過生物或統計方式，都沒有明確固定的迴路定義。

cues.en: For example, and this is actually a counter example, this diagram depicts an electronic circuit.
cues.zh: 例如，其實這是個反例，這張圖畫的是電子電路。

cues.en: Now in this case we know exactly what this circuit is and how it works because humans invented this.
cues.zh: 這個情況，我們精確知道它是什麼、如何運作，因為是人類發明的。

cues.en: But that is not the kind of circuit that just naturally emerges on its own.
cues.zh: 但那不是自然自行浮現的迴路，

cues.en: This is specifically crafted for a specific purpose.
cues.zh: 而是為特定目的，刻意設計的。

cues.en: These other three images here highlight different circuits that we can talk about in another complex system, which is the brain.
cues.zh: 另外三張圖，則凸顯另一個複雜系統，也就是大腦中，可討論的不同迴路。

cues.en: So this one here depicts a neuron.
cues.zh: 這張畫的是神經元。

cues.en: So the black lines here, all these thin black lines here.
cues.zh: 這些黑線，全部這些細黑線，

cues.en: This depicts a tracing of a single brain cell.
cues.zh: 描繪一個腦細胞的形狀。

cues.en: The soma or the body is down here.
cues.zh: 胞體位於下面，

cues.en: And all of these little ramifications are lots of dendrites that form connections to other neurons around the basal area.
cues.zh: 這些小分枝，都是許多樹突，在基底區與其他神經元形成連結。

cues.en: And then there's this main dendritic branch coming up here, connecting to yet more neurons at the apical sites.
cues.zh: 接著有這條主要樹突分枝，往上延伸，在頂端位置連接更多神經元。

cues.en: Now, the thing is that even within a single brain cell, there are subcomponents of the cell that form
cues.zh: 問題是，即使單一腦細胞內，也有細胞子元件，形成

cues.en: their own mini circuits, and they can implement their own individual computations such as logical operations, correlation, detection, filtering, and amplification.
cues.zh: 自己的小型迴路，執行個別計算，例如邏輯運算、相關偵測、濾波與放大。

cues.en: In other words, we can talk about circuits in the brain at a subcellular level.
cues.zh: 換句話說，可以從次細胞層級，討論腦中的迴路。

cues.en: And then we have this higher level of anatomical organization here where each of these, like gooey little triangles now depicts a neuron.
cues.zh: 接著，更高一層的解剖組織，這些軟軟的小三角形，每個表示一個神經元，

cues.en: So these are the cell bodies.
cues.zh: 也就是細胞體。

cues.en: And now we can talk about how neural circuits form comprising a few dozen or maybe a few hundred neurons that are collectively implementing one kind of computation.
cues.zh: 現在可以討論，由幾十或幾百個神經元組成、共同執行某種計算的神經迴路。

cues.en: And there's an even higher level where we can talk about interactions between different brain regions as forming a circuit for some high level cognitive or behavioral process.
cues.zh: 再更高一層，也能將不同腦區之間的互動，視為執行高階認知或行為過程的迴路。

cues.en: And now we are talking about circuits that include millions or billions of neurons.
cues.zh: 這時討論的迴路，就包含幾百萬、幾十億個神經元。

cues.en: Of course, there is a theme that ties all of these levels of description together, which is that the
cues.zh: 當然，有個主題串起所有描述層級，就是

cues.en: individual components of a system work together towards some common computational goal.
cues.zh: 系統的個別元件，共同朝某個計算目標運作。

cues.en: But my point here is that there's no real precise anatomical definition or way of confidently measuring the boundaries of an anatomical circuit in the brain.
cues.zh: 但重點是，沒有真正精確的解剖定義，也沒有能有把握地測量腦中解剖迴路邊界的方法。

cues.en: That is true for nervous systems, and it's true for really any complex system.
cues.zh: 這對神經系統成立，對幾乎任何複雜系統也成立。

cues.en: And how about in deep learning models?
cues.zh: 那深度學習模型呢？

cues.en: Now what you see here, this diagram, this is not an LM architecture but just a more general multilayer feed forward model.
cues.zh: 這裡這張圖，不是語言模型架構，只是一般多層前饋模型。

cues.en: So what would a circuit look like that is embedded inside this network?
cues.zh: 嵌入這個網路中的迴路，會長什麼樣子？

cues.en: Perhaps these four units here are all working together.
cues.zh: 也許這裡四個單元一起合作，

cues.en: Maybe they're all strongly correlated, and their combined output is crucial for some kind of feature detection in the data.
cues.zh: 可能高度相關，而且合併輸出，對資料中的某種特徵偵測很關鍵。

cues.en: And maybe this is a little circuit with only two units over here.
cues.zh: 也許這裡是一個只有兩個單元的小迴路，

cues.en: Or maybe all six of these units form a circuit that spans multiple layers.
cues.zh: 或者全部六個單元，形成跨越多層的迴路。

cues.en: And because the weights and the activations are continuous numbers in these deep learning models, it's
cues.zh: 而且，因為這些深度學習模型的權重與活化是連續數值，

cues.en: just never going to be the case that we can identify circuits simply by looking at what neurons are active at the same time and which ones aren't.
cues.zh: 所以永遠不會只看哪些神經元同時活躍、哪些沒有，就能辨識迴路。

cues.en: And that's because unless you have an extremely robust L1 regularizer or you're using dropout during
cues.zh: 因為除非有非常強的 L1 正規化，或者學習時使用

cues.en: learning, then every neuron in the entire network has some non-zero activation.
cues.zh: dropout，否則整個網路的每個神經元，都有某個非零活化。

cues.en: And even if it has a negative activation that gets shunted by ReLU non-linearity, there still won't be any neurons that have zero input.
cues.zh: 即使有負活化，被 ReLU 非線性阻斷，仍不會有輸入為零的神經元。

cues.en: Here you see another diagram of what a circuit in a language model might look like, at least conceptually.
cues.zh: 這裡另一張圖，顯示語言模型迴路可能的樣子，至少概念上如此。

cues.en: So this shows that circuits are not necessarily fixed in the model.
cues.zh: 它顯示，迴路不一定在模型中固定不變，

cues.en: They can evolve over time as new tokens are processed and more information is aggregated.
cues.zh: 隨著新 token 被處理、更多資訊被彙整，可能逐漸演變。

cues.en: Conceptually, this is a beautiful idea that circuits are not fixed but instead are fluid over time.
cues.zh: 概念上，這是很漂亮的想法，迴路不固定，而是隨時間流動。

cues.en: But that makes for extremely difficult and nuanced data approaches to actually identify and characterize
cues.zh: 但這讓真正辨識、描述迴路，

cues.en: those circuits, and also confirming the statistical robustness of the existence of those circuits in large data sets.
cues.zh: 以及在大型資料集確認其存在的統計穩健性，所需資料分析方法，變得極困難、細膩。

cues.en: So it just becomes really tricky to make sure that you're not just identifying some weird quirk that happens to emerge in one particular text sequence.
cues.zh: 因此，要確保自己找到的，不只是某個特定文字序列碰巧浮現的怪現象，就非常棘手。

cues.en: So yeah, all of this stuff is very tricky for multiple reasons.
cues.zh: 這些事情，確實因多種原因而非常難。

cues.en: Here I have a very loose definition of a circuit in a deep learning network.
cues.zh: 這裡對深度學習網路中的迴路，提出一個非常寬鬆的定義。

cues.en: This is an operational definition in the sense that it's like a guiding principle for thinking about analysis methods that I will introduce you to in this section.
cues.zh: 它是操作性定義，也就是思考本章分析方法時的一項指導原則。

cues.en: Please do not interpret this statement to Restrictively.
cues.zh: 請不要過度嚴格地解讀這個說法，

cues.en: This is not meant to be a formal scientific definition.
cues.zh: 它不是正式的科學定義。

cues.en: Basically, the analysis that I will introduce you to in this section are focused on using statistical
cues.zh: 基本上，本章介紹的分析，著重於使用統計

cues.en: techniques to identify neurons or dimensions that behave in similar ways.
cues.zh: 技巧，找出行為方式相似的神經元或維度。

cues.en: I hope I didn't come across as being too negative or pessimistic about identifying circuits in complex systems like LMS.
cues.zh: 希望對於在 LLM 這類複雜系統中辨識迴路，我沒有顯得太負面或悲觀。

cues.en: This kind of research is very difficult, but I think it's one of the most exciting and promising avenues of interpretability in complex systems.
cues.zh: 這種研究非常困難，但我覺得，是複雜系統可解釋性中，最令人興奮、最有前景的方向之一。
